claims.text: Cryogenic rolling introduces a controlled amount of lattice distortion into eutectic high-entropy alloys.
Cryogenic rolling promotes the formation of nanoscale twins.
Cryogenic rolling promotes the formation of dislocation networks.
Nanoscale twins and dislocation networks act as barriers to dislocation movement.
Obstruction of dislocation movement increases strength and resistance to plastic deformation.
Preservation of a degree of crystallographic order during cryogenic rolling maintains ductility.
Cryogenic rolling can simultaneously increase strength and ductility in eutectic high-entropy alloys.
The proposed intervention is cryogenic rolling at -196 °C with a 30% reduction in area.
The proposed treatment is expected to increase yield strength by 15% relative to the as-cast alloy.
The proposed treatment is expected to increase elongation at break by 20% relative to the as-cast alloy.
The intervention requires an alloy composition within the eutectic region.
The effectiveness of the intervention diminishes when the composition deviates significantly from the eutectic region.
The effectiveness of the intervention diminishes if rolling introduces excessive defects.
Grain refinement may contribute to the mechanical-property changes caused by cryogenic rolling.
The relationship between the amount of lattice distortion and the resulting mechanical properties is not well established.
